q1: How much table tennis have you played at a club, in a league or with a coach (casual ping-pong at home, at work or on holiday doesn't count)?
q1a: None yet — only casual ping-pong, or a handful of club sessions.
q1b: Less than a year, or only now and then.
q1c: 1 to 2 years, about once a week or more.
q1d: More than 2 years of regular play, now or in the past.
q2: Have you played tennis, badminton, squash, padel or another racket sport?
q2b: Yes, casually or a long time ago.
q2c: Yes, regularly for a year or more.
q2d: Yes — in leagues, club teams or tournaments.
q3: Rallying — which is closest to you?
q3a: I'm still learning to keep the ball on the table, or I rally by hitting flat and miss most balls that carry backspin or topspin.
q3b: I can keep a forehand-to-forehand rally going at moderate pace; my backhand is less reliable, and when I push a backspin ball it often goes high or into the net.
q3c: I keep medium-paced rallies going on both forehand and backhand, and push backspin balls back low and consistently; switching quickly between the two sides still causes errors.
q3d: I rally at a good pace on both sides, move my feet to switch between forehand and backhand, and can push short or long and choose where it goes.
q4: Serving — which is closest to you?
q4a: My serve just starts the rally — little or no spin.
q4b: I can put backspin or sidespin on my serve, but it often bounces high or long and gets attacked.
q4c: I have at least two different spin serves that I keep low, and I win a few points directly from my serve.
q4d: I vary spin and length with a similar-looking action (short backspin, no-spin, fast long serves) and plan to attack the return.
q5: Returning serves — which is closest to you?
q5a: Spin serves often fly off my bat or go into the net; I can't tell what spin is on the ball.
q5b: I return simple serves, but heavy backspin or sidespin often catches me out; I mostly just push or block the ball back.
q5c: I return most serves at club sessions by adjusting my bat angle for backspin or topspin; sidespin and no-spin serves still cause some errors.
q5d: I read most serves from the server's bat and choose my return — a short push, a flick, or a topspin against long serves — so the server rarely gets an easy attack.
q6: Attacking with topspin (loops) and blocking — which is closest to you?
q6a: I don't loop yet; when someone hits a topspin attack at me, the ball usually flies off my bat.
q6b: I hit through high, easy balls, but against backspin I can only push; when someone hits a strong topspin attack at me, I rarely get it back on the table.
q6c: I can forehand-loop a long backspin ball (such as a long push) in most attempts, and block some medium-paced loops back onto the table.
q6d: I loop consistently against both backspin and topspin on my forehand, can also open up with my backhand, and block or counter-hit most loops.
q7: Which games do you usually play, and how do they go?
q7a: Mostly casual hitting, practice drills or coaching — I rarely play scored games against club players.
q7b: Friendly scored games with other beginners at a club or social session.
q7c: Regular club sessions or a lower league division; I win about half my games against club regulars.
q7d: League or tournament matches where I win at least half; at the club I usually beat intermediate players.
